findings.claim: A folder crumb can be a link even when choosing it shows the same view as the current position. folderCrumbs tests whether the segment's view differs from the target's top (narrowFolders(targetFolders, segment) vs targetFolders), not whether it differs from the current view (narrowFolders(targetFolders, position)).
findings.impact: Under a Smart Collection with more than one path (for example path:A/b/c path:Q) at position A/b, the crumb A is a link. Choosing it pushes a history entry and scrolls to the top, but the requests (folder=[A/b/c]), the shelves, the chips and the crumb trail stay the same. You can reach this position in normal use by pressing Back across a target change (spec §1.6 keeps the old position), or by opening a URL you saved earlier. The effect is small.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/appshell/folderPosition.ts:70 sets `link: strictAncestor && !sameFolders(narrowFolders(targetFolders, folder), targetFolders)`. folders.ts:26-40 narrowFolders keeps a target folder inside the segment and drops any target folder outside it. So narrowFolders([A/b/c, Q], A) = [A/b/c] ≠ T (A becomes a link), and narrowFolders([A/b/c, Q], A/b) = [A/b/c], which is the current view. The chip loader (readingapp/LibraryFace.tsx:117-128, videoapp/LibraryFace.tsx:119-129) sends folder=[A/b/c] at both positions, so base and chips are the same. searchQuery.ts:674-677 accepts several path: terms, and videoAppTarget.ts:43 passes them as params.folder. The revised I8 (r6) still requires that every folder crumb link 'goes to a strict ancestor of the position whose view differs from the current one'.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Trace: target query 'path:A/b/c path:Q', URL ?folder=A/b. targetFolders=[A/b/c,Q], folders=[A/b/c], base=A/b/c, end=A/b/c, segments A (strict ancestor; narrow(T,A)=[A/b/c]≠T → link), A/b (position, plain), A/b/c (current). Choosing A gives position A with folders=[A/b/c], so every request is the same. No test uses a target with more than one folder. If line 70 compared with narrowFolders(targetFolders, position), the sf-videos case at appFolderPosition.test.tsx ('a segment above a folder-limited target's folder is plain') would still pass; that is why the tests cannot tell the two rules apart.

bucket_proposal.reason: The revised I8 says a folder crumb link must go to a view that differs from the current one. With a target of two folders, the code renders a link whose view is the same.

findings.proposed_fix: Make a folder crumb a link only when narrowFolders(targetFolders, segment) differs from both targetFolders and narrowFolders(targetFolders, position). Add a position test with a target of two path: folders.

specification_compliance: The fix since r6 (e51492d4e) changes only documents: invariants.md revises I8 so that the home crumb is a link whenever the URL holds a `folder`. The code already does this (FolderPositionRows.tsx:61-75 renders an <a> whenever position !== null), so the r6 finding I8-TOP no longer conflicts with the invariant in force.

I8's folder-crumb clause ('whose view differs from the current one') is implemented as 'differs from the target's top' (folderPosition.ts:70). That is spec §1.5's wording. The two agree for single-folder and no-folder targets and disagree for targets with several folders (I8-FOLDER-SAME).

The implementation notes hold. The page drops target and folder in one replace from one snapshot of the search params (useFolderPositionUrl.ts:50-57). Both shelf routes drop folder and from_folder when a target is chosen (video/shelf/page.tsx:63-82, reading/shelf/page.tsx:63-82). Video See all links carry folder only when position !== null (videoapp/LibraryFace.tsx:231-232).

I2: blocked = empty || (position !== null && folders.length === 0). This disables the chip loader, tag candidates, grouped and flat requests in both faces (videoapp/LibraryFace.tsx:128-211, readingapp/LibraryFace.tsx:127-213).
I14: useFolderChips.ts:100 draws a held answer only when its loader matches the current loader.

Home shortcut: in useVideoApp.ts:183-199, the target-handled effect runs in the same commit that clears pendingId. While a target is pending, params is null, so no request carries the old folder before droppedAt takes effect.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The revised I8 says the home crumb is a link 'whenever the URL holds a folder'. While an invalid `folder` is still in the URL (before the replace from I10 lands), or while droppedAt masks the folder, position is null. Under a folder-limited target the crumbs are then drawn from base with a plain home crumb. This lasts one render.

VideoShelfPage counts URL folders in filtersActive (VideoShelfPage.tsx:172-177). An empty See all page opened from a position therefore shows 'Nothing matches these filters' rather than the no-files state. This carries over from r6 and is still open for a person.
regression_risks: No product code changed since r6, so the r6 regression notes still apply. e2e-components fixtures that mount the Video LibraryFace (for example videoCardSpacing) now also receive a by=folder shelf_limit=24 chip request and draw a chip row.
Video's control-row spacing on a coarse pointer depends on pointer-coarse:mb-3 at videoapp/LibraryFace.tsx:245. Only e2e-components/folder-rows.spec.ts guards it.
test_coverage: No test uses a target with several path folders. The folder-crumb link rule in folderPosition.ts:70 cannot be told apart from the 'differs from current' alternative by the existing tests.
folderPosition.ts (readFolderPosition, folderCrumbs) has no unit test. It is covered only through the route-level tests in appFolderPosition*.test.tsx.
appFolderPosition.test.tsx asserts the home crumb as a link under sf-math at Videos/Study, which matches the revised I8.
not_verified: I did not run vitest, Playwright or the app. Every observation comes from reading the files.
I did not confirm from the backend (shelves.py) that several `folder` values are ORed. I assumed this from the frontend narrowing code and the spec.
I did not read the raw diff of commit e51492d4e itself. Its content was inferred from the commit subject, r7/fixes.txt and invariants.md.
I read only the diff hunks of the existing Reading and Video test files, not their unchanged parts.
trajectory: The only fix since r6 is e51492d4e, and it changes only documents. It revises I8 in invariants.md so that the home crumb is a link whenever the URL holds a `folder`, which is what the code already did. That resolves r6's I8-TOP by changing the invariant rather than the code. The round adds no new branch, state or prediction to the product code and removes none, so it does not show the design being patched in code. The folder-crumb clause of the revised I8 still says 'differs from the current one', while the code compares with the target's top. That leftover mismatch is reported here as I8-FOLDER-SAME.
